title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 explains Lagrange's 1768 method for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y. Lagrange introduces an auxiliary time t, with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = −√Y, and passes to second differentials. Euler first runs the degenerate (genus-0) case dx/(a+2bx+cx²) + dy/(a+2by+cy²) = 0. Lagrange's procedure gives an integral of the form F(x,y)/(a−cxy)² = C.

Page 11 does three things.

(1) It finishes the check for the example a=1, b=1/2, c=1 begun in §21–22. The arctan route gives α = (1−xy)/(x+y+xy) = const. Lagrange's route gives β = (1+x+y)/(1−xy) = const. Since 1/α = (x+y+xy)/(1−xy), one has β − 1/α = 1, so the two integrals agree up to the constant.

(2) Euler observes from the examples that the general Lagrange-type integral factors as (2b+c(x+y))(a(x+y)+2bxy)/(a−cxy)² = C.

(3) §23 reduces this to the simplest form. Put P = (2b+c(x+y))/(a−cxy) and Q = (a(x+y)+2bxy)/(a−cxy). Then aP − cQ = 2b(a−cxy)/(a−cxy) = 2b identically, so Q = (aP−2b)/c. Hence PQ = (aP²−2bP)/c = const forces P itself to be constant. The integral therefore becomes (2b+c(x+y))/(a−cxy) = C, or equivalently Q = C.

§24 announces that this simplest form can be reached directly, without second differentials. The next page does this with p = x+y and u = xy: dp/(2b+cp) = q dt = du/(cu−a). In modern terms, the integral is the symmetric (1,1)-correspondence 2b + c(x+y) + C(cxy − a) = 0. This is the addition law for the arctangent / Möbius-type integral of a quadratic denominator, i.e. the genus-0 analogue of Euler's symmetric biquadratic addition relation.
errors: No mathematical errors. aP − cQ = [2ab + ac(x+y) − ac(x+y) − 2bcxy]/(a−cxy) = 2b is correct.
The general factorization specializes correctly to (1+x+y)(x+y+xy)/(1−xy)² for a=1, b=1/2, c=1.
Minor gap: the step 'a quadratic in P is constant, hence P is constant' needs a continuity/connectedness remark (P could in principle jump between the two roots). This is standard and harmless.

ideas.what: Factorization of the integral from Lagrange's method in the quadratic (Riccati-type separated) case, and reduction of the product of two invariants to a single invariant via the linear relation aP − cQ = 2b
ideas.modern_name: First integral / addition law of the genus-0 separated equation; symmetric bilinear (1,1) correspondence
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Nova Acta Acad. Petrop.); also Euler's earlier treatment of addition theorems in Institutiones calculi integralis I

ideas.what: Comparison of the arctan-derived integral with Lagrange's integral, showing they differ only by a functional change of constant (β = 1 + 1/α)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine verification and simplification of the elementary (rational/arctan) case of Lagrange's method, within a well-known paper. The reduction is algebraically neat but trivial and fully published.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image well; no substantive corrections needed.
